We propose tracking AI progress over time using the task completion time horizon: the duration of tasks that models can complete at a certain success probability, providing an intuitive measure of real-world capability compared to humans.
All tasks are automatically scored with a continuous score or binary threshold; details of how we normalize and process scores are given in Section 3.1, and other task suite details in Appendix B.

To convert agent run data to task completion time horizon, we first convert the agent performance on each task to a binary value (success or failure). Many tasks are naturally binary, including all SWAA tasks.

Continuously scored tasks are binarized via a task-specific threshold chosen to represent human performance. For HCAST, the task-specific threshold is the same “target score” the human baseliner tries to achieve, which we also use to filter for successful runs.
